newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian police charge two Frenchmen with spying.
newsitem.headline: Indian police charge two Frenchmen with spying.

text.p: Indian federal police on Monday indicted two Frenchmen and two Indians for spying by allegedly carrying out illegal underwater surveys that could aid an enemy in anti-submarine warfare.

K.P. Satheesan, a lawyer for the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), told Reuters the charges, including alleged violations of the Official Secrets Act, were filed with the chief judicial magistrate in the southern port of Cochin.

The two French accused, Francois Clavel and Philippe Elle, were crew members from the catamaran "Galathee". They were arrested in January 1995 by harbour police for allegedly carrying out an unauthorised survey of the seabed near Cochin, site of a major Indian naval base. An Indian businessman and a former Indian politician were also charged.

Elle recently told Reuters that the survey was meant to determine if the harbour was suitable for aquaculture and could serve as a base for pleasure sailing. The "Galathee" crew was also interested in studying a 16th-century ship wreck, he said.

The six members of the vessel's crew, five French nationals and a cook from Madagascar, were held in custody for five months. They were granted bail last June but have been required to stay in Cochin.

Satheesan, speaking to Reuters in New Delhi over the telephone from Cochin, said the charge sheet accused the four of criminal conspiracy to collect sensitive data on the seabed using sophisticated equipment.
The CBI counsel, reading the charge sheet, said the data might be "directly or indirectly useful to an enemy" and "caused security risk to Indian naval operations".
Satheesan said the type of studies carried out by the crew, whom he said were aided by the businessman and former politician, "are important for anti-submarine warfare".
Asked if the CBI was accusing the four of spying, Satheesan said: "Yes." He said the charges carried a maximum prison sentence of seven years.
Lawyer Ajay Malarkandy, who is representing the six crew members, said Clavel and Elle denied the charges.
"This is out of thin air," Malarkandy said. "I'm amazed that someone who does a bottom profile about eight miles off Cochin is looking out for anti-submarine warfare."
